<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
The birth multiset of a PD $\mathcal{D}_q (X)$ is defined as $\mathcal{B}_q (X)=\{b\mid (b,d)\in \mathcal{D}_q(X), d-b\geq\epsilon\}$, i.e., the multiset containing all the prominent birth scales \footnote{Birth scales of the topological features with extremely small persistence, i.e., noises, are not considered here.} in $\mathcal{D}_q (X)$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
Given points $X_\mathcal{M}$ sampled from manifold $\mathcal{M}$ and non-empty homology dimension range $Q=\{q_1,q_2,...\}$, for $q\in Q$, topologically irrelevant points $X_\mathrm{ir}^q$ are the maximal subset $\hat{X}\subset X_\mathcal{M}$ such that $\mathcal{B}_{q}(X_\mathcal{M})=\mathcal{B}_q (X_{\mathcal{M}}\setminus\hat{X})$. And the corresponding topologically relevant points are $X_\mathrm{r}^q=X_\mathcal{M} \setminus X_\mathrm{ir}^q$, i.e., $\mathcal{B}_q(X_\mathcal{M})=\mathcal{B}_q(X_{\mathrm{r}}^q)$. Combining all homology dimensions, we have the (aggregated) topologically relevant points $X_\mathrm{r}=\bigcup_{q\in Q}X_\mathrm{r}^q$ and topologically irrelevant points  $X_\mathrm{ir}=\bigcap_{q\in Q} X_{\mathrm{ir}}^{q}$.
    \label{def:topological-relevance}
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
Under Definition~\ref{def:topological-relevance}, the topologically relevant and irrelevant points form a decomposition of \(X_{\mathcal M}\), i.e., $X_{\mathcal M}=X_{\mathrm{r}}\cup X_{\mathrm{ir}}, X_{\mathrm{r}}\cap X_{\mathrm{ir}}=\varnothing.$
\label{proposition:topological-relevance}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
Given a point cloud
$X=\{x_i\}_{i=1}^n\subset\mathbb R^d$, a sample size $m$, and target
homology dimensions $Q$, Topology Recovery Task asks for selecting a landmark
set $S\subset X$, $|S|=m$, such that the PDs computed on $S$ can serve as
a faithful surrogate for the PDs of the unknown topologically relevant signal
$X_r$.
\label{definition:TRP}
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
The q-th Hodge Laplacian $L_q$ of $\mathcal{K}$ is a square matrix $L_q\in\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{K}_{q}|\times |\mathcal{K}_{q}|}$ indexed by the q-simplices of $\mathcal{K}_q$: $        L_q = B_{q-1}^\top B_{q-1} + B_{q}B_{q}^\top$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
For a simplicial complex $\mathcal{K}$, let $L_q$ be the Hodge Laplacians
and $\beta_q$ be the Betti numbers of $\mathcal{K}$. We have that
$\mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{ker}(L_q)) = \beta_q$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
Under Definition 2, 
the topologically relevant and irrelevant points form a partition of \(X_{\mathcal M}\), i.e., $X_{\mathcal M}=X_{\mathrm{r}}\cup X_{\mathrm{ir}}, X_{\mathrm{r}}\cap X_{\mathrm{ir}}=\varnothing.$
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By definition, for every \(q\in Q\),
\[
X_{\mathrm{r}}^q = X_{\mathcal M}\setminus X_{\mathrm{ir}}^q.
\]
Therefore, we have
\[
X_{\mathrm{r}}
=
\bigcup_{q\in Q}X_{\mathrm{r}}^q
=
\bigcup_{q\in Q}\left(X_{\mathcal M}\setminus X_{\mathrm{ir}}^q\right).
\]
We now show that
\[
\bigcup_{q\in Q}\left(X_{\mathcal M}\setminus X_{\mathrm{ir}}^q\right)
=
X_{\mathcal M}\setminus \bigcap_{q\in Q}X_{\mathrm{ir}}^q.
\]
For any point \(x\), we have
\[
x\in \bigcup_{q\in Q}\left(X_{\mathcal M}\setminus X_{\mathrm{ir}}^q\right)
\]
if and only if there exists some \(q\in Q\) such that
\[
x\in X_{\mathcal M}
\quad\text{and}\quad
x\notin X_{\mathrm{ir}}^q.
\]
Since \(X_{\mathcal M}\) does not depend on \(q\), this is equivalent to
\[
x\in X_{\mathcal M}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\exists q\in Q,\ x\notin X_{\mathrm{ir}}^q.
\]
The second condition is equivalent to
\[
x\notin \bigcap_{q\in Q}X_{\mathrm{ir}}^q.
\]
Thus, we have
\[
x\in X_{\mathcal M}
\quad\text{and}\quad
x\notin \bigcap_{q\in Q}X_{\mathrm{ir}}^q,
\]
which means
\[
x\in X_{\mathcal M}\setminus \bigcap_{q\in Q}X_{\mathrm{ir}}^q.
\]
Hence, it holds that
\[
X_{\mathrm{r}}
=
X_{\mathcal M}\setminus \bigcap_{q\in Q}X_{\mathrm{ir}}^q.
\]
Using the definition
\[
X_{\mathrm{ir}}=\bigcap_{q\in Q}X_{\mathrm{ir}}^q,
\]
we can obtain
\[
X_{\mathrm{r}}=X_{\mathcal M}\setminus X_{\mathrm{ir}}.
\]
Finally, we have
\[
X_{\mathrm{r}}\cup X_{\mathrm{ir}}
=
\left(X_{\mathcal M}\setminus X_{\mathrm{ir}}\right)\cup X_{\mathrm{ir}}
=
X_{\mathcal M}.
\]
and 
\[
X_{\mathrm{r}}\cap X_{\mathrm{ir}}
=
\left(X_{\mathcal M}\setminus X_{\mathrm{ir}}\right)\cap X_{\mathrm{ir}}
=
\varnothing.
\]
Thus, \(X_{\mathrm{r}}\) and \(X_{\mathrm{ir}}\) form a partition of
\(X_{\mathcal M}\).
<!-- end proof-1 -->
